newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - July 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - July 15.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Foreign Minister Prachuab Chaiyasan will leave for Beijing tomorrow for talks with Cambodia's King Norodom Sihanouk as part of Association of Southeast Asian Nations' (ASEAN) efforts to defuse the conflict between Cambodia's leaders. Prachuab will join Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas and the Philippines' Domingo Siazon for discussions with the ailing king on Second Prime Minister Hun Sen's violent coup on July 5, which ousted First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh. (THE NATION, BANGKOK POST)

- Immigration police have been ordered to make sure owners of the Royal Jomtien Resort Hotel do not leave the country as investigations into the fatal fire get under way. There are three groups of people who could face legal action following last Friday's fire in which 90 people, among them 11 foreigners, were killed. (BANGKOK POST)

- Chaiwat Sinsuwong will be asked today to resign as Palang Dharma head to make way for a new leader election in two months. Nearly 200 district and city councillors from the party will today submit a letter demanding Chaiwat's resignation at the party headquarters. (BANGKOK POST)

- The National Economic and Social Development Board (NESDB) insists that the eighth plan will go ahead and is vowing to reassert itself as the country's top planning agency, to provide marco-economic guidelines to politicians in office. The agency has recommended freezing the minimum wage this year, warning that a pay hike would accelerate and send inflation out of control. (THE NATION)

- Nava Finance and Securities, a subsidiary of Thai Military Bank, will purchase two ailing finance firms - Prime Finance and Securities and Thana One Finance and Securities - in its effort to get a banking license. Nava says it will enter purchase and assumption agreements with six companies. (BUSINESS DAY)

- Small- and medium-scale commercial banks have moved quickly to rebut market rumours of financial weakness and possible collapse. The Bank of Asia and Siam City Bank issued unaudited first-half performance figures yesterday to the Stock Exchange of Thailand, with both showing slight improvements in profits from 1996. Analysts say the banks moved to announce figures early in response to the market rumours. (BANGKOK POST)
